subject: Post-call: capabilities matrix & integration actions (SDK, funcall, streaming, embeddings)
messages:
From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: Elaine Chen <elaine@novamed.ai>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-22T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: capabilities matrix & integration actions (SDK, funcall, streaming, embeddings)

Hi Elaine —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment heading into the POC: 

High-level pain / goals you confirmed
- Existing triage assistant returns generic answers and can't reference patient context (EHR snippets).
- Latency spikes during burst hours cause timeouts in your current reranker; cost is a concern at scale.
- You need deterministic structured outputs for downstream systems (FHIR-like JSON) and a clear safety/regression guardrail process.

What Redwood can do (summary)
- SDK + function-calling: We'll provide a lightweight SDK change to map Novamed intent slots directly to function calls. That reduces prompt engineering and improves reliability for structured outputs.
- Streaming + graceful fallback: Continuous token streaming with a KV-prefix cache to hit your 200–300ms SLO for short responses, and automatic fallback to a smaller quantized variant under load.
- Embedding + rerank pipeline: We recommended a hybrid approach — production embeddings for recall, lightweight neural reranker for precision; batch-friendly endpoints to cut token costs.
- Eval & monitoring: Will include a small prompt set for quality regression checks and per-route latency/cost dashboards in the console.

Concrete next steps (action items)
1) I’ll share a short POC plan and a capabilities matrix that maps Novamed requirements to Redwood features (attached).
2) Your team to confirm top-3 representative prompts (triage + discharge + med-ask) and one dataset slice we can use for warmup (non-PHI or de-identified).
3) Schedule 60-min technical deep-dive with your engineering and infra lead next week — suggested slots Wed/Thu.

Attachments: novamed-poc-plan.pdf (POC scope, success criteria), capabilities-matrix.xlsx (feature mapping)

If that aligns, I’ll put the technical-deep-dive invite on the calendar once you confirm availability.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: Elaine Chen <elaine@novamed.ai>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novamed.ai
Date: 2026-11-22T17:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: capabilities matrix & integration actions (SDK, funcall, streaming, embeddings)

Hi Marcus —

Appreciate the clear recap. This matches our takeaways. A couple of clarifications before we share prompts: 

- For the structured outputs we need explicit schema validation (FHIR-lite) on the function-call response. Can your SDK enforce/return a JSON schema validation error so our downstream worker can reject and log failures?
- Regarding de-identified warmup data: we can provide a small batch (~1k rows) of synthetic examples by Monday.
- Deep dive: Thu 2026-11-26 10:00–11:00 PT works for our infra lead (Samir). I’ll confirm after procurement reviews the POC scope.

Procurement note (cc): we may ask for a short pilot contract (30 days) with a capped spend and an SLA on throughput — will follow up formally.

Thanks,
Elaine Chen
Head of Product Integrations | Novamed
elaine@novamed.ai

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: Elaine Chen <elaine@novamed.ai>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-22T18:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: capabilities matrix & integration actions (SDK, funcall, streaming, embeddings)

Thanks Elaine — short answers inline below, and added a follow-up item list.

- JSON schema validation: yes — our SDK can run a strict JSON Schema validation step post-function-call and return a structured error payload (error_code, schema_path, example_payload). We’ll include that in the POC contract as an acceptance criterion.
- Synthetic dataset: great — please send the sanitized sample to poc@redwood.com. We’ll confirm receipt and run a warmup embedding job.
- Pilot contract: understood. We’ll propose a 30-day pilot with a spend cap and a throughput SLA; procurement can redline as needed.

Follow-up items (I’ll action)
- Send meeting invite for Thu 11/26 10:00–11:00 PT and include a short agenda (tech scope, infra reqs, acceptance tests).
- Upload the POC playbook and capabilities matrix to the shared Drive link (see metadata).
- Prepare a minimal SDK patch for function-call schema enforcement and a streaming config that meets your SLOs for the deep dive demo.

Attachments referenced in Drive: novamed-poc-plan.pdf, capabilities-matrix.xlsx

Speak soon — I’ll send the calendar invite after procurement confirms the time.

Best,
Marcus

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: monica.patel@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-24T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap — prep for Novamed deep-dive (internal)

Forwarding the Novamed thread — action items we own before Thu: 

- Monica: draft the SDK change set that adds JSON Schema validation to function-call responses; include a test harness and a rollback plan if schema mismatches rise above threshold. Estimate: 3 dev days.
- Jonas: outline streaming config (batching window, kv-cache TTL, smaller-variant fallback policy) and cost/latency tradeoffs for the deck. Prepare perf numbers on 8xA100 and 4xH100 profiles.
- I’ll draft the 30-day pilot SOW and the acceptance criteria (schema validation + latency p95 target + cost cap).

We should also include a short slide showing the rerank architecture (embeddings for recall, neural reranker for precision) and clear handoff points for Novamed to own once the POC completes.

Let me know if either of you need help or want to split tasks.

Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
